title: BHMAP comprehensive validation results

provenance_note: Exact checks prove the finite identities they test. Numeric checks are falsification attempts (no counterexample found, not a proof). Toy checks illustrate the abstract logic. Online checks compare citations with Crossref/arXiv. This is machine re-checking of the supplied construction, not human verification or independent replication.

results.name: The other (inequivalent) 5D Clifford irrep Γ⁴ → −Γ⁴: is the witness structure representation-dependent?
results.method: rebuild model with Γ⁴ sign flipped
results.claim: robustness information (not a claim of the paper)

details.interpretation: Γ⁴ → −Γ⁴ is not a similarity: it switches to the other 5D irrep (sign of the Clifford volume element). Agreement = evidence the witness structure survives in the second irrep; disagreement = representation dependence of the fixed background data. Neither outcome affects the result in the paper's irrep (core §2). Not required to agree.

results.name: Lemma 4.1 (oscillatory H⁻¹ bound, m = 1): ‖e^{iΛk·y}g‖_{H⁻¹} ≤ 2(Λ|k|)⁻¹‖g‖ + 4(Λ|k|)⁻²‖D²g‖, d = 1,2,4; compact C^∞ and Gaussian families; grid-refinement record
results.method: FFT on periodic boxes; compactly supported bumps (primary) and Gaussians (supplementary); many Λ, k; refinement n → 2n
results.expected: max ratio ≤ 1 in both families; refinement change < 1e-3

details.norm_note: H¹ = L² + ‖∇‖² (R1 v2 convention); H⁻¹ weight (1+|ζ+Λk|²)⁻¹ applied with an exact shift; ‖D²g‖² = ∫|ζ|⁴|ĝ|². This is the FULL-SPACE H⁻¹(ℝ^d) norm of the zero extension, which is ≥ the local H⁻¹(B′) norm (more test functions), so a full-space pass is the stronger statement. Not an equality with the local norm.

results.name: Ball geometry: B_d(y₀,ρ) ⊂ B_e(y₀,2ρ) ⊂ V′ and B_e(y₀,ρ/3) ⊂ B_d(y₀,ρ) for ρ ≤ π/6; d(y,y₁) ≤ 3|y−y₁| on V′; 9/4 ≤ μ ≤ 9; ¼I ≤ g ≤ 9I
results.method: exact closed-form geodesic distance on S²(1)×S²(3), random sampling

analytic.argument: g ≥ ¼I ⇒ a curve leaving V′ from y₀ has Euclidean length ≥ π/3 hence g-length ≥ π/6, so for ρ ≤ π/6 every point of B_d(y₀,ρ) is reached inside V′ by a curve of Euclidean length < 2ρ ⇒ B_d ⊂ B_e(2ρ) ⊂ V′; g ≤ 9I and convexity of V′ ⇒ d(y,y₁) ≤ 3|y−y₁| (straight segment) ⇒ B_e(ρ/3) ⊂ B_d(ρ). The sampling above tests the implementation of these facts.

details.scope: random sampling detects implementation errors; it does not prove the inclusions — the analytic argument does

results.name: BT2 + density: exact vol_μ(B_d(y₀,ρ)) is continuous, strictly increasing; Monte-Carlo with μ = 9 sinθ₁ sinθ₂ matches it
results.method: closed-form volume on S²(1)×S²(3) vs Monte-Carlo in the chart
results.expected: strictly increasing, continuous; |z| < 5 for MC vs exact

details.argument: V′(ρ) = ∫₀^ρ 36π² sinα₁ · sin(√(ρ²−α₁²)/3) · ρ/(3√(ρ²−α₁²)) dα₁ has a positive integrand on (0, ρ) for 0 < ρ ≤ π/6, so V is C¹ (hence continuous) and strictly increasing; the sampled values illustrate this.
